newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's MobilCom plans bourse listing in March.
newsitem.headline: Germany's MobilCom plans bourse listing in March.

text.p: German mobile telephone firm MobilCom AG plans to list its shares on the Frankfurt stock exchange in March as part of the bourse's new growth stock initiative, the head of its IPO consortium said Wednesday.

Frankfurt-based DG Bank said investors would be offered some 640,000 five-mark par value shares in MobilCom, Germany's largest independent mobile phone services provider, in a bookbuilding period to run March 4-6.
The listing would follow on March 10, the launch date for the bourse's so-called "New Market" segment, which is designed to help young, technologically innovative firms to go public.
Bourse officials said last month they hoped as many as 15 firms would take part in the scheme this year and that a full German growth stock index could begin late in 1998.

Five years old and active in a sector considered one of Germany's most dynamic, MobilCom achieved pre-tax profit of some 12 million marks ($7.3 million) in 1996 on sales of around 269 million, and is expecting high growth rates in 1997 and 1998, DG Bank said in a statement.
New Market is aimed specifically at companies which are potentially interesting to certain investors but lack the history or capital to go it alone with an IPO.

Under the scheme, companies are required to fulfil strict conditions on issue conditions and transparency to reduce the risk attached to them, but in return receive help and publicity from the bourse.
In addition, each company will have a "guardian" -- a role similar to a market maker and generally taken by the issuing bank -- who will guarantee to provide buy and sell prices on the stock.
Such firms often find it difficult to drum up enough investor interest in the over-the-counter market to which their shares are normally confined.
